trajectory.thought: The leader is a seeded baseline (median of full pool) and the verdict is "indistinguishable" — the runner-up is not statistically better. The diagnosis explicitly favours a robust combination given unstable rankings and high error correlation, and the median is exactly that. With only 3 validation windows, fitted weights carry high variance and are unlikely to beat the robust median. I should accept.

action_args.justification: The series has strong trend and seasonality with unstable model rankings (Kendall tau 0.212) and high inter-model error correlation (mean 0.834, only 3 independent groups). Under these conditions, a robust median over the full pool is the natural choice: it is insensitive to the few models that spike in any given window, and it avoids the high-variance weight estimation that only 3 validation windows can support. The leader is a seeded baseline and the runner-up is statistically indistinguishable, so accepting is the correct stopping decision.
